standard_prerequisites.use: They guarantee that the associated primes of the tensor products $N \otimes_R Q$ are contained in the set of associated primes of the modules $N \otimes_R \kappa(\mathfrak p)$, so the hypothesis of the criterion is met.

core_obligations: Read the hypotheses supplied by the statement: both rings Noetherian, $N$ a finite $S$-module and flat over $R$ (statement lines 2108-2112).

Verify the hypothesis of the general criterion, using the Bourbaki lemma and remark to bound the associated primes of the tensor products by those of the fibres, where the stated condition on $\mathfrak q$ with $IS + \mathfrak q \neq S$ applies (proof lines 2122-2129).
Conclude universal injectivity of $N \to N^\wedge$ as a map of $R$-modules (proof lines 2117-2118).
proof_roadmap: Bounding associated primes by those of the fibres (proof lines 2122-2129).
Conclusion from the general criterion (proof line 2123).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a flatness-flavoured sufficient condition for the map from a finite module into its $I$-adic completion to be universally injective over the base: the associated primes of the fibres must avoid the ideal after extending to $S$ (statement lines 2102-2119). The proof reduces it to the general criterion by invoking the Bourbaki results that control associated primes of tensor products through those of the fibres. The reduction of the hypothesis to the fibrewise condition is the substance, so the claim is H2.
